title: Alarm Performance (EEMUA 191 / ISA-18.2)
description: Retrospective alarm-system performance against EEMUA 191 targets. Read-only: this dashboard does not acknowledge, shelve, or suppress anything, and is not a substitute for the operator alarm banner in the HMI.

options.content: EEMUA 191 targets: **< 6 alarms/operator/hour** (long-term target ~1), **< 10 alarms per 10-minute window**, **< 1% of time in flood**, and the **top 10 alarms should account for < 5%** of total load. Exceeding these is an alarm-rationalisation finding, not a process fault. A red panel here means the alarm system needs review, not that the plant is unsafe.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('1 hour', ts) AS time,
       count(*)::float AS "alarms/hour"
FROM event_log
WHERE event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

panels.title: Peak alarms per 10 minutes (EEMUA target < 10)
panels.description: Windows above 10 are alarm floods. Sustained floods are the condition under which operators stop reading alarms at all.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT time_bucket('10 minutes', ts) AS time,
       count(*)::float AS "alarms/10min"
FROM event_log
WHERE event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 1

WITH windows AS (
  SELECT time_bucket('10 minutes', ts) AS bucket, count(*) AS n
  FROM event_log
  WHERE event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY 1
)
SELECT 100.0 * count(*) FILTER (WHERE n >= 10) / NULLIF(count(*), 0)
       AS "flood %"
FROM windows

SELECT count(*)::float
       / NULLIF(EXTRACT(EPOCH FROM ($__timeTo()::timestamptz - $__timeFrom()::timestamptz)) / 3600.0, 0)
       AS "alarms/hour"
FROM event_log
WHERE event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(ts)

SELECT CASE severity
         WHEN 0 THEN 'Low (normal)'
         WHEN 1 THEN 'Medium (Hi/Lo)'
         WHEN 2 THEN 'High (HiHi/LoLo)'
         ELSE 'Unclassified'
       END AS metric,
       count(*)::float AS value
FROM event_log
WHERE event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(ts)
GROUP BY 1
ORDER BY 2 DESC

panels.title: Top 10 bad actors (should be < 5% of total load)
panels.description: The classic alarm-rationalisation starting point. In most unrationalised plants a handful of tags generate the majority of alarms; fixing those has more effect than anything else.

targets.rawSql:
WITH total AS (
  SELECT count(*)::float AS n
  FROM event_log
  WHERE event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(ts)
)
SELECT e.description        AS "Alarm",
       t.name               AS "Tag",
       count(*)             AS "Count",
       round(100.0 * count(*) / NULLIF((SELECT n FROM total), 0), 1)
                            AS "% of load"
FROM event_log e
LEFT JOIN tag_definition t ON t.id = e.tag_id
WHERE e.event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(e.ts)
GROUP BY e.description, t.name
ORDER BY count(*) DESC
LIMIT 10

panels.title: Chattering alarms (repeat within 60 s)
panels.description: An alarm that re-fires within a minute of clearing is almost always a deadband or filtering problem, not a real repeated excursion.

targets.rawSql:
WITH gaps AS (
  SELECT description,
         ts,
         lag(ts) OVER (PARTITION BY description ORDER BY ts) AS prev_ts
  FROM event_log
  WHERE event_type = 'ALARM' AND $__timeFilter(ts)
)
SELECT description AS "Alarm",
       count(*)    AS "Rapid repeats"
FROM gaps
WHERE prev_ts IS NOT NULL
  AND ts - prev_ts < INTERVAL '60 seconds'
GROUP BY description
ORDER BY 2 DESC
LIMIT 10

panels.title: Alarms with no acknowledge within 24 h (standing/stale)
panels.description: EEMUA target is ~zero standing alarms. A permanently active alarm trains operators to ignore the banner.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT a.ts          AS "Raised",
       a.description AS "Alarm",
       t.name        AS "Tag",
       a.severity    AS "Severity"
FROM event_log a
LEFT JOIN tag_definition t ON t.id = a.tag_id
WHERE a.event_type = 'ALARM'
  AND $__timeFilter(a.ts)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM event_log k
    WHERE k.event_type = 'ACKNOWLEDGE'
      AND k.tag_id IS NOT DISTINCT FROM a.tag_id
      AND k.ts > a.ts
      AND k.ts < a.ts + INTERVAL '24 hours'
  )
ORDER BY a.ts DESC
LIMIT 200

panels.title: Alarms raised while the tag had no valid sample
panels.description: Detection control for the class of defect where a non-finite reading drives alarm state. An alarm whose tag has no finite sample within +/- 5 s of the event is suspicious and should be investigated. Empty is the expected result.

targets.rawSql:
SELECT e.ts          AS "Event",
       e.event_type  AS "Type",
       e.description AS "Alarm",
       t.name        AS "Tag"
FROM event_log e
JOIN tag_definition t ON t.id = e.tag_id
WHERE e.event_type IN ('ALARM', 'ACKNOWLEDGE')
  AND $__timeFilter(e.ts)
  AND NOT EXISTS (
    SELECT 1 FROM tag_sample s
    WHERE s.tag_id = e.tag_id
      AND s.ts BETWEEN e.ts - INTERVAL '5 seconds'
                   AND e.ts + INTERVAL '5 seconds'
  )
ORDER BY e.ts DESC
LIMIT 200
